searchText: <@301186049323958275> i've been working on a "relay monitor" to run these sorts of validations: https://github.com/ralexstokes/relay-monitor and there is work to support the relay monitor API into mev-boost so that we can use the info to disable bad relays Does it work even if the relays are 100% malicious/actively attacking via the most clever way possible? https://github.com/flashbots/mev-boost/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+relay+monitor i have had my hands full w/ a few other things recently but trying to get something shipped to coincide w/ devcon 🙂 you can see a live deployment of the flashbots sepolia relay here: https://sepolia.relay-monitor.pbs.dev i haven't added any of the logic to do the validations but that is last piece before an acceptable v1 i think we need to be specific about various attacks somethings are not attributable and that information can be derived by the relay monitor and passed to mev-boost, which must then decide what to do w/ the information I meant generally are you deriving all of your data from trustless sources, or are you asking the relay to tell you things and trusting it isn't lying? ah the former the relay APIs are great but i don't think we can rely on them for security purposes so instead, the relay monitor looks at any data it gets via public APIs from relays and (for those mev-boost users who opt-in) can get signed auction "transcripts" all of this data can be correlated with data on-chain to get a good idea of what is happening there is still some stuff where it is hard to say who is at fault, but the fault can be surfaced and then we can add increasingly sophisticated policy logic to mev-boost over time to figure out how to deal with it Anything that surfaces inconsistencies would make me happier than the current situation. I feel like at the moment everyone is just saying "one can theoretically verify some of what the relay is saying" but no one currently does it (except maybe <@144468805697929216> it sounds like, which is reassuring). i agree 🙂 it can be stochastic and it only needs to be sufficiently likely even if so to bias relay/builder incentives sufficiently towards honest on average if they don't know which responses <@144468805697929216> will check, that might suffice
